requirements.title: A 4B-8B pretrained semantic backbone is integrated

verification.notes: Qwen/Qwen3-4B at the pinned revision is loaded, frozen (4,022,468,096 parameters counted independently, all requires_grad=False, bf16), used for embeddings (multi-depth pooled, cached, cache invalidated on adapter updates) and for generation; A's 6 GPU tests pass; load 6-13 s, 7.804 GB. Not checked: Qwen3-8B (never loaded). Numerical caveats of bf16 operation: generation log-probabilities are accurate to 0.1-0.3 nats per token only (defect D3), an embedding depends on batch composition at the 1 % level (D8).

requirements.limitations: [A] Qwen/Qwen3-4B (4,022,468,096 parameters, bf16, frozen, pinned revision) is the only backbone loaded and tested; Qwen3-8B is a configuration change that was not run. Texts longer than max_text_tokens are cut to head 3/4 + tail 1/4 (counted in backbone.stats), not chunked. Single-stream generation speed is bounded by per-step Python overhead on this shared machine (on par with transformers' own generate, measured).

requirements.title: Shared high-dimensional latent representations function

verification.notes: Verified on the real configuration: shapes / dtypes of the tensor contract, exact causality, padding / batch / candidate / query independence, time conditioning, persistent state, value channel (cos(+1,-1) <= 0.19 for texts of 1-380 tokens; held-out linear probe recovers asinh(value) from the token with R^2 0.993 and from b with 0.997), z depends on b / action / goal, gradients of z / phi / generation losses reach experiential weights, LoRA and bridge with magnitudes confirmed by finite differences. Gaps: (1) phi is not well-conditioned on real inputs at initialisation (Gram max/min eigenvalue 5.4e4 over 2304 real combinations, 1.9e6 for a single query; the unit test uses white-noise inputs) - D6; (2) candidates that differ only in an argument are almost identical in z (cos 0.9997 for click e3 vs e4) - D7; (3) text -> belief depends on batch composition at 1.4 % on the bf16 backbone - D8; (4) whether the representations become useful abstractions after training is not shown here (A states this too).

requirements.limitations: [A] Verified at initialisation and on small synthetic learning problems (8-step recall); whether the representations become useful abstractions is a question for training on real experience (Workstreams D / S). phi is bounded (unit norm) but NOT well-conditioned on realistic inputs at initialisation: real configuration, 2304 realistic combinations: Gram max/min eigenvalue 2.3e4, 90 % of the mass in 23 of 128 directions; one query alone 4.5e5 (participation ratio 2.0). The float64 fast layer stays exact on such features (tested). Candidates that differ in one argument: cos(z) 0.747 on Qwen3-4B (was 0.9997); one of several argument leaves changing moves z less (bag of leaves).

requirements.title: Fast numerical adaptation functions (Gaussian and non-Gaussian likelihoods)

verification.notes: Exact where checked: Gaussian known-noise and normal-inverse-gamma recursions equal independent float64 closed forms to 1e-15, surprises sum to the exact log marginal likelihood, order invariance, Joseph form stays PSD over 50k collinear updates, GLM Laplace updates (count / binary / time-to-event with censoring) equal a reference solution to 4e-15 for moderate data, predictive NLL equals brute-force quadrature, forgetting / change detection behave as stated, calibration on synthetic data. Refuted: (D1, major) the Newton iteration is not converged for observations far below the prior predictor - time-to-event censored at 30 days in seconds gives a rate 1.86x too high, at one year 13.5x with a surprise of 192 instead of 122 nats, count 0 with exposure 1e9 339x; the training path online_nll (6 steps) fails already for a mode 6 nats below the prior; (D2) the count dispersion tempers binary and time-to-event updates; (D4) NIG predict() under-states the predictive variance by a/(a-1); (D5) impossible observations (negative count, successes > trials, negative time) are absorbed.

requirements.limitations: [A] One posterior per outcome kind (real, count, binary, time-to-event); categorical outcomes are not modelled by the fast layer (change request A-5). Non-Gaussian updates are Laplace approximations: the mode is exact (monotone safeguarded search to |step| <= 1e-11 (1 + |eta|), cap 100 iterations, measured <= 7 iterations for counts / time-to-event and <= 16 for 1e9 binomial trials; iterations and convergence are returned), the shape is Gaussian. Time-to-event uses a constant-hazard (exponential) likelihood. The learned dispersion exp(disp_raw) (1 at init) tempers count likelihoods only. Inferred-noise Gaussian: predict() returns the Student-t predictive variance (b/(a-1))(1+q); posterior()['cov'] / ['noise'] are the scale (b/a)V and b/a. Impossible observations raise ValueError (stateful update and online_nll).

requirements.title: Experiential weights receive real learning gradients

verification.notes: Experiential weights receive real gradients through D's ContinualLearner. Debug scale (CPU): one frequent update changes experiential + heads tensors, adapters and reward untouched (reward tensors carry no .grad), behaviour probe moves (max |dz| 0.017). Real configuration (Qwen3-4B + 50m core, CUDA, own parameter snapshots): 127 experiential and 56 head tensors changed, 0 adapter / 0 reward tensors, frozen backbone hash unchanged (checked in a fresh process), predictions moved (max |db| 1.32, |dNLL| 0.064); grad norm experiential 0.425 (D: 0.344), weight delta 0.2540 (D: 0.2529). Not shown by anyone: a learning curve on the real configuration (D says so).

requirements.limitations: [D] Shown at debug scale (tiny random backbone, debug core) on LabWorld diagnostic experience, and as single updates on Qwen3-4B + the 50m core. No learning curve exists for the real configuration and none on live experience. The prediction loss used in D's evidence is D's local wrapper of Workstream B's stage-1 world heads. Held-out mean NLL 2.981 -> 2.291 (change -0.690 +- 0.259 SE, n=151); the median did not improve (1.902 -> 2.106) and 0.50 of the held-out records improved: the gain is in the over-confident tail. The learner is not yet called by agent.py.

requirements.title: Semantic adapters receive real learning gradients

verification.notes: Mechanism verified on the real backbone: all 72 LoRA modules receive finite non-zero gradient through the embedding path (tokens -> core -> z / phi) and through generation_logprob; with the backbone in float32 finite differences match the analytic gradient to < 1 % for LoRA-B at initialisation, for all LoRA A/B and bridge tensors away from it, and for a loss on z via tokenize / encode_actions / encode_goals(with_grad=True); the bf16 gradients used in operation have cosine 0.995-0.999 and norm ratio 0.975-0.999 against float32; checkpointing on/off gives identical gradients; frozen weights never get gradient; one optimizer step changes embeddings and generation. Gap (stated by A as well): updates of the adapters driven by real experience are the slow schedule of workstream D and are not exercised by this lens.

requirements.limitations: [A] Shown on Qwen3-4B: all 72 LoRA modules and every bridge tensor receive gradient through the embedding path and through generation_logprob, and with the backbone loaded in float32 central finite differences along the analytic gradient equal its norm to 3 % for every path (embedding -> LoRA-B, generation -> LoRA-B, -> zero-init bridge, -> latent, -> all adapters, -> bridge -> b -> experiential weights). generation_logprob / the sampler use a float32 output layer (head error on the same hidden states 0.0000 nats, was up to 0.143); the bf16 decoder trunk still differs from the float32 model by up to 0.36 nats on a one-token completion, and the KV-cache sampler differs from generation_logprob by up to 0.073 nats per token. Caches follow the adapter content (also .data writes). NOT shown here: adapter updates driven by real experience (Workstream D's schedule).

requirements.title: Experience tokens for every item kind; exact values preserved alongside embeddings

verification.notes: to_items covers every contract record type and all 17 item kinds (A's test passes); TokenBatch.values carries exact float64 values (1e15+1, a denormal, the largest double); the separate value channel keeps numbers visible beside texts of any length (cos(+1,-1) <= 0.19, cos(1e15,-1e15) 0.11, zero vs missing 0.72, 3 vs 4 0.65); non-finite quantities are dropped and counted; more than 4 quantities continue in further items via to_items and are dropped-but-counted when passed to tokenize directly. Values 0.1 % apart (1000 vs 1001) are indistinguishable in the embedding (cos 0.99999) and exist exactly only in TokenBatch.values.

requirements.limitations: [A] A token carries at most max_values (4) quantities; to_items continues longer lists in further items, while the candidate-action encoder keeps the first 4 cost quantities (dropped ones are counted in tokenizer.stats). Action targets / arguments: up to 16 leaves through the value channel (numbers exact + hashed identity of every leaf), further leaves dropped and counted (stats['dropped_arguments']). Metric names are hashed into 2 x 2048 buckets (collisions possible). Relations and entities are text items; there is no graph structure.

requirements.title: Trainable conditioning from CAM's latent state into semantic action generation

verification.notes: Latent bridge on Qwen3-4B: bit-identical logits / log-probabilities / generations with and without a latent at initialisation (latent norms 1e-3..1e3), non-zero gradient on the zero-initialised output projections at step 0 (finite differences 1.002 in float32), one Adam step changes the generated text and makes the next-token distribution depend on the latent (TV 0.42 between latent and -latent), 40 bridge-only steps make two latents produce two different answers while the unconditioned output is unchanged, and the generation loss reaches the experiential weights through latent=b (finite differences 0.996). Not shown: that a bridge trained on experience improves candidate actions (A states this); credit/providers.py detaches the latent it passes.

requirements.limitations: [A] The bridge is cross-attention from the decoder's residual stream to bridge_tokens virtual prefix tokens, not tokens placed in the sequence (a literal zero prefix is not a no-op: measured logit change up to 1.0469; change request A-2). Shown: exact no-op at init, non-zero gradient, and that one optimisation step makes next-token probabilities depend on the latent. NOT shown: that a trained bridge improves the quality of generated candidate actions (needs training on experience; Workstreams B / D).

requirements.title: Bayesian adaptation compared against recurrent adaptation and simple statistical baselines

verification.notes: The comparison (learned-prior Bayes vs exact BLR on raw inputs vs GRU vs running statistics, Gaussian and count targets, training and held-out families) exists and is reproducible: a full-length rerun of seed 0 reproduces every recorded per-seed number (mean and per-support NLL and RMSE, 4 methods x 2 targets x 2 splits) with zero difference at 4 decimals. The failures are reported: worse than the GRU below 3 observations, fixed-noise variant fails on held-out families, count margin over the GRU -0.018 nats (seed 0 alone: -0.0186 +- 0.0105, z = -1.76). Not stated in the status file: on held-out Gaussian families the GRU has the lower RMSE (0.8185 vs 0.8629). Synthetic tasks only. Robustness check with stronger GRUs (seed 0): the held-out verdict holds (GRU 128/8000: 1.9264, GRU 256/16000: 1.3825, learned prior 0.8907; counts 2.6306 vs 2.6132, inside the noise), but the in-distribution lead of the learned prior does not (GRU 256/16000: 0.1825 vs 0.2206). The noise-mode ablation of seed 0 also reproduces exactly (fixed noise 1.9935 on held-out families).

requirements.limitations: [A] See scientific_failures for where the learned prior loses (small support on Gaussian targets; fixed-noise variant; point accuracy on held-out Gaussian families; in-distribution ranking against a larger GRU; only a marginal lead on held-out counts). Synthetic meta-regression only (2-d inputs, 4 training and 3 held-out function families, 2 seeds, 600 evaluation tasks per split); it says nothing yet about real experience. The significance figures pool tasks that share one trained model per seed. Re-run with the converged GLM updates and the count-only dispersion (exp(disp_raw), 1 at init): Gaussian numbers unchanged to 4 decimals; count numbers changed (the BLR baseline, a Laplace GLM, improved most). Verdicts: {"gaussian": "held-out families: winner = learned_prior_bayes; ranking = ['learned_prior_bayes', 'blr_raw', 'gru', 'running_stats']; learned prior WINS", "count": "held-out families: winner = learned_prior_bayes; ranking = ['learned_prior_bayes', 'gru', 'blr_raw', 'running_stats']; learned prior WINS"}

verification.notes: Sandboxed terminal execution is real (as root; dedicated-uid camsbx, Landlock ABI1, seccomp). Generated code runs as uid 996 and could not: read /root, a root-owned 0600 file, the camauth vault file, another process's /proc/environ, /etc/shadow; open a socket or connect to loopback; escape via .. or a symlink; write outside the workspace or to /tmp; regain privileges via setuid(0). A fork bomb and unbounded allocation are stopped with leftover=0; a spawned child does not outlive its program (p11, 16 checks). Scoped network: every outbound connection is one authorizer call before resolution, a refused host never connects, loopback is refused even when the authorizer says yes (p12). Process isolation on a shared kernel, not a VM, as documented.

requirements.limitations: [EC] Process isolation on the shared host kernel (dedicated uid + rlimits + Landlock ABI 1 + seccomp + no_new_privs), not a VM. Memory is limited per process by RLIMIT_AS; the total of a job and its task count are watched by the per-job monitor every 100 ms (no cgroup available). Disk use is bounded per file and checked against a workspace limit before each operation, not by a quota. Jobs under the same sandbox uid can signal each other. Scoped network: the kernel denies every socket; outbound TCP goes through the egress broker with one ExecContext.check per connection (host, port) made before name resolution; requests reusing a connection and anything inside TLS are not inspected; only Python processes get the transparent shim (curl, git, node have no network). Importable packages inside the sandbox: standard library, numpy, PIL, yaml. multiprocessing locks do not work (/dev/shm is not granted). Not exercised against workstream EA's real policy service or over ExecRPC.
